headline: Hawaiian Teen's Coconut Fungi Discovery Could Clean Ocean Plastic and Sunscreen
meta_description: Kaiser High School senior Vera Wang discovered fungi in coconut husks that can biodegrade ocean plastics and sunscreen, winning multiple science fair awards.
summary_short: A Hawaiian high school student found that fungi naturally living on coconut husks can break down sunscreen and microplastics—and may have discovered a new species.
body:
Vera Wang, a senior at Kaiser High School in East Honolulu, discovered that fungi naturally inhabiting coconut husks can biodegrade both sunscreen and plastic pollutants from ocean water. Working in Anthony Amend's lab at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Wang designed and built a sustainable ocean filter made entirely from coconut byproduct waste—inspired by traditional Polynesian weaving methods. Her breakthrough research earned her multiple awards at the Hawaiʻi State Science & Engineering Fair, including first place in the Microbiology category and a scholarship from the McInerny Foundation. The discovery may include previously uncharacterized fungal species, as genetic testing revealed organisms with no match in the world's largest reference database of known genes and genomes.

Wang's journey began during her sophomore year, but the real innovation came when she realized that removing pollutants from water was only half the problem. The remaining challenge was responsible disposal—which led her to investigate whether coconut husks could do more than physically capture waste. She learned that the pore structure of coconut fiber creates a favorable environment for microbial growth, prompting her to explore the fungal communities already living there. By studying their degradation abilities on sunscreen and plastic media, Wang and her team identified a tannin compound that indicates which fungi possess the ability to biodegrade these pollutants.

Wang's work has qualified her for the International Science & Engineering Fair taking place next May in Arizona. She credits graduate student Kaylee Christensen and Professor Amend for making the research possible. "My research would have never, ever, been possible without Anthony and Kaylee," Wang said. Amend noted that her success reflects the strength of Hawaiʻi's public school system and expressed optimism about the discoveries she will make in college.
quick_facts: Kaiser High School senior in East Honolulu discovered ocean-cleaning fungi
Filter made from coconut waste inspired by Polynesian weaving traditions
Fungi may be previously unknown species, not in any genetic reference database
Won first place in Microbiology and qualified for International Science Fair in Arizona
